newsitem.title: USA: Suspended crude loadings resume at Valdez terminal.
newsitem.headline: Suspended crude loadings resume at Valdez terminal.

text.p: Crude oil loadings, suspended briefly out of Alaska's Valdez terminal due to high winds, resumed early this morning, a marine officer said.
"The port was not closed but we stopped loading because of the weather," a marine operations officer with Alyeska Pipeline contacted early Thursday said.
Two crude oil tankers were affected by the suspension, which went into effect at 1600 Alaska time/1600 GMT, but loadings resumed early this morning.
"It's not unusual stopping operations at this time of year. We do it whenever the weather presents a problem to safety," the marine officer added.
The pipeline carries about 1.47 million barrels per day (bpd) of crude oil from fields in Alaska's North Slope region.
Alyeska Pipeline Service Co is the consortium that operates the 800-mile line and the Valdez terminal.
